cell.title: Cell
cell.author: Stephen King
cell.why: A zombie-phone apocalypse novel that readers name as one of King's weakest.

dreamsnake.title: Dreamsnake
dreamsnake.author: Vonda N. McIntyre
dreamsnake.why: A healer travels a post-apocalyptic world with her snakes; an older, unique and well-made science fiction novel.

lord fouls bane.title: Lord Foul's Bane
lord fouls bane.author: Stephen R. Donaldson
lord fouls bane.why: First book of the Thomas Covenant chronicles, about a leper pulled into a fantasy land; a famously difficult antihero fantasy.

lud in the mist.title: Lud-in-the-Mist
lud in the mist.author: Hope Mirrlees
lud in the mist.why: A staid merchant town borders Fairyland and a smuggling mystery; an early, whimsical fantasy classic.

non stop.title: Non-Stop
non stop.author: Brian W. Aldiss
non stop.why: A generation starship's descendants have forgotten they are on a ship; a classic of the genre.

unmaking of june farrow.title: The Unmaking of June Farrow
unmaking of june farrow.author: Adrienne Young
unmaking of june farrow.why: A woman investigates her mother's disappearance and a family curse; a romantic fantasy mystery that readers read quickly.

cat who saved books.title: The Cat Who Saved Books
cat who saved books.author: Sosuke Natsukawa
cat who saved books.why: A talking cat guides a boy through fantastical labyrinths to save books; short, warm and Ghibli-like.

ones company.title: One's Company
ones company.author: Ashley Hutson
ones company.why: A lonely woman lives inside her favourite TV show; lovely absurdist fiction.

wings of fire.title: Wings of Fire
wings of fire.author: A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
wings of fire.why: The comments recommend a different Wings of Fire (the dragon series), so the entry does not match the Kalam book.

city and its uncertain walls.title: The City and Its Uncertain Walls
city and its uncertain walls.author: Haruki Murakami
city and its uncertain walls.why: A man is drawn into a mysterious walled city; late Murakami with his usual dreamlike strangeness.

stranger beside me.title: The Stranger Beside Me
stranger beside me.author: Ann Rule
stranger beside me.why: A true-crime author tells of her friendship with the serial killer Ted Bundy; a classic of the genre.

fun home.title: Fun Home
fun home.author: Alison Bechdel
fun home.why: A graphic memoir about the author's father, family and coming out; critically loved.

hardwired.title: Hardwired
hardwired.author: Walter Jon Williams
hardwired.why: A cyberpunk adventure of a smuggler and a pilot in a corporate future; a solid genre favourite.

tales of the city.title: Tales of the City
tales of the city.author: Armistead Maupin
tales of the city.why: Quirky characters share a San Francisco apartment building in the 1970s; funny, light and loved.

dead inside.title: Dead Inside
dead inside.author: Chandler Morrison
dead inside.why: An extreme transgressive horror novel mentioned mostly as shocking, not as a praised read.

dark eden.title: Dark Eden
dark eden.author: Chris Beckett
dark eden.why: Descendants of stranded colonists survive on a dark, cold planet; winner of the Arthur C. Clarke Award.

jesus and john wayne.title: Jesus and John Wayne
jesus and john wayne.author: Kristin Kobes du Mez
jesus and john wayne.why: A history of how white evangelical America embraced militant masculinity; readers recommend it for insight into politics and religion.

bartleby the scrivener.title: Bartleby, the Scrivener
bartleby the scrivener.author: Herman Melville
bartleby the scrivener.why: A clerk who answers every request with 'I would prefer not to'; a short, famous story.

stay true.title: Stay True
stay true.author: Hua Hsu
stay true.why: A Pulitzer-winning memoir about friendship, grief and growing up in the 1990s.

state of wonder.title: State of Wonder
state of wonder.author: Ann Patchett
state of wonder.why: A scientist travels into the Amazon to find a mentor and her secret drug research; an easy read with deeper themes.

hunchback of notre dame.title: The Hunchback of Notre-Dame
hunchback of notre dame.author: Victor Hugo
hunchback of notre dame.why: A deformed bell-ringer, a gypsy girl and a priest in medieval Paris; a long classic that readers recall from youth.

our missing hearts.title: Our Missing Hearts
our missing hearts.author: Celeste Ng
our missing hearts.why: A boy searches for his mother in a near-future America that bans dissent; striking and unsettling.

have always lived in the castle.title: We Have Always Lived in the Castle
have always lived in the castle.author: Shirley Jackson
have always lived in the castle.why: Two sisters live in isolation after a family poisoning; a classic of eerie psychological gothic.

patriot.title: Patriot
patriot.author: Alexei Navalny
patriot.why: The Russian opposition leader's memoir, with his life, politics and fight against Putin.

wayward.title: Wayward
wayward.author: Chuck Wendig
wayward.why: Sequel to Wanderers, in which survivors rebuild after a pandemic; readers like the series.

bartimaeus trilogy.title: The Bartimaeus Trilogy
bartimaeus trilogy.author: Jonathan Stroud
bartimaeus trilogy.why: A snarky djinni serves a young magician in an alternative London; a funny, clever YA fantasy trilogy.

before and after.title: Before and After
before and after.author: Andrew Shanahan
before and after.why: A story of life in a world where overweight people are hunted; readers found it very different and well developed.

unruly.title: Unruly
unruly.author: David Mitchell
unruly.why: A funny, informative romp through English monarchs by the comedian; readers find it informative and hilarious.

romantic comedy.title: Romantic Comedy
romantic comedy.author: Curtis Sittenfeld
romantic comedy.why: Comments split between those who couldn't put it down and a reader who finished it just to criticise it.

requiem for a dream.title: Requiem for a dream
requiem for a dream.author: Hubert Selby, Jr.
requiem for a dream.why: Four people spiral through addiction in Brooklyn; a harrowing, unforgettable novel.

iron dragons daughter.title: The Iron Dragon's Daughter
iron dragons daughter.author: Michael Swanwick
iron dragons daughter.why: A girl enslaved in a dragon factory in a grim fantasy-industrial world; a harsh, subversive fantasy classic.

behave.title: Behave
behave.author: Robert M. Sapolsky
behave.why: A neuroscientist traces human behaviour from a split second to evolutionary time; heavy but widely praised, even on audio.

gate to womens country.title: The Gate to Women's Country
gate to womens country.author: Sheri S. Tepper
gate to womens country.why: In a post-apocalyptic world women run walled cities while men live apart; a provocative, discussed feminist novel.

tiny beautiful things.title: Tiny Beautiful Things
tiny beautiful things.author: Cheryl Strayed
tiny beautiful things.why: A collection of advice-column letters answered with warmth and honesty by 'Sugar'; readers find it healing.

supermarket.title: Supermarket
supermarket.author: Bobby Hall
supermarket.why: Comments are split, with one reader abandoning it quickly and another praising it as a short read.

yearbook.title: Yearbook
yearbook.author: Seth Rogen
yearbook.why: A comedian's collection of funny stories from his life and career rather than a straight autobiography.

rangers apprentice.title: Ranger's Apprentice
rangers apprentice.author: John Flanagan
rangers apprentice.why: A boy apprenticed to a ranger learns spycraft and archery in a medieval-style world; a series that got many readers hooked.

joyland.title: Joyland
joyland.author: Stephen King
joyland.why: A student working at a summer amusement park investigates an old murder; readers say it made them cry.

war and remembrance.title: War and remembrance
war and remembrance.author: Herman Wouk
war and remembrance.why: Follows a family through the second half of World War II; a sprawling saga that teaches readers a great deal.

authority.title: Authority
authority.author: Jeff VanderMeer
authority.why: Second book in the Southern Reach trilogy, following a new director of the agency studying Area X.

motherless brooklyn.title: Motherless Brooklyn
motherless brooklyn.author: Jonathan Lethem
motherless brooklyn.why: A detective with Tourette's syndrome tries to solve his boss's murder in Brooklyn; stylish noir.

orphan masters son.title: The Orphan Master's Son
orphan masters son.author: Adam Johnson
orphan masters son.why: A man rises through North Korea's brutal system; read quickly and widely praised.

paris.title: Paris
paris.author: Paris Hilton
paris.why: Mentioned among 'rough' audiobook picks rather than as a praised book.

hard times.title: Hard Times
hard times.author: Charles Dickens
hard times.why: Dickens' short novel attacking a cold, fact-obsessed industrial town.

heart goes last.title: The Heart Goes Last
heart goes last.author: Margaret Atwood
heart goes last.why: A couple joins a prison-sharing community in a collapsing economy; Atwood with a Black Mirror feel.

city of saints and madmen.title: City of Saints and Madmen
city of saints and madmen.author: Jeff VanderMeer
city of saints and madmen.why: Linked tales, documents and appendices from the strange city of Ambergris; weird fiction at its best.

joseph and his brothers.title: Joseph and his brothers
joseph and his brothers.author: Thomas Mann
joseph and his brothers.why: Mann's retelling of the biblical story of Joseph; dense, philosophical and rich.

split tooth.title: Split Tooth
split tooth.author: Tanya Tagaq
split tooth.why: An Inuk throat singer's mix of memoir, myth and poetry, set in the Arctic; unusual and powerful.

nevermoor.title: Nevermoor
nevermoor.author: Jessica Townsend
nevermoor.why: A cursed girl finds a hidden magical city and a place in a special society; loved by younger readers.

orchid thief.title: The Orchid Thief
orchid thief.author: Susan Orlean
orchid thief.why: A reporter follows a flamboyant orchid hunter in Florida; a quirky and observant nonfiction classic.

darkness outside us.title: The Darkness Outside Us
darkness outside us.author: Eliot Schrefer
darkness outside us.why: Two rivals on a spaceship race to save the Earth and find a secret; a fast, emotional YA sci-fi.

drawing of the three.title: The Drawing of the Three
drawing of the three.author: Stephen King
drawing of the three.why: Roland of the Dark Tower pulls three people from our world; the book that fans call one of the best fantasies.

seven year slip.title: The Seven Year Slip
seven year slip.author: Ashley Poston
seven year slip.why: A woman's apartment lets her meet a man across seven years; a cute and easy time-slip romance.

natural beauty.title: Natural Beauty
natural beauty.author: Ling Ling Huang
natural beauty.why: A woman working in an elite beauty-clinic discovers something unnatural; a modern horror-satire.

vladimir.title: Vladimir
vladimir.author: Julia May Jonas
vladimir.why: A campus novel of a professor's obsession; readers are split, with one calling it awful.

everything i know about love.title: Everything I Know About Love
everything i know about love.author: Dolly Alderton
everything i know about love.why: A memoir on friendship, dating and growing up in your twenties; funny and relatable.

nobodys fool.title: Nobody's Fool
nobodys fool.author: Richard Russo
nobodys fool.why: A stubborn small-town man in upstate New York; a warm, sardonic character study.

teacher.title: The Teacher
teacher.author: Freida McFadden
teacher.why: A popular thriller, but the comments mostly criticise the writing style.

hours.title: The Hours
hours.author: Michael Cunningham
hours.why: Three women in different eras linked by Mrs Dalloway; a short, moving novel readers stay obsessed with.

ohio.title: Ohio
ohio.author: Stephen Markley
ohio.why: Four former classmates return to their declining Ohio town in one night; a slow-unfolding novel about America.

spillover.title: Spillover
spillover.author: David Quammen
spillover.why: Quammen tracks how animal viruses jump to humans; an informative and gripping epidemic read.

ascension.title: Ascension
ascension.author: Nicholas Binge
ascension.why: A mysterious mountain appears in the ocean, drawing a woman into its mysteries; praised even by Stephen King.

seven deaths of evelyn hardcastle.title: The Seven Deaths of Evelyn Hardcastle
seven deaths of evelyn hardcastle.author: Stuart Turton
seven deaths of evelyn hardcastle.why: A man relives one day in many bodies to solve a murder; a clever, puzzle-like mystery.

witchs heart.title: The Witch's Heart
witchs heart.author: Genevieve Gornichec
witchs heart.why: A witch from Norse myth lives on in a story of love and loss; recommended retelling.

house next door.title: The House Next Door
house next door.author: Anne Rivers Siddons
house next door.why: A house on a quiet street slowly ruins its occupants; a quiet haunted-house classic.

science.title: Bad Science
science.author: Ben Goldacre
science.why: The comments do not discuss this book, so the match is wrong.

vampires of el norte.title: Vampires of El Norte
vampires of el norte.author: Isabel Cañas
vampires of el norte.why: A vampire story set in 1840s Mexico, mixing romance and horror; readers praise its romance.

friends lovers and the big terrible thin.title: Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing
friends lovers and the big terrible thin.author: Matthew Perry
friends lovers and the big terrible thin.why: The actor's honest memoir of fame and addiction; frank and moving.

creep.title: Creep: Accusations and Confessions
creep.author: Myriam Gurba
creep.why: Essays on the author's life, abuse and rage, with sharp humour.

shake hands with the devil.title: Shake hands with the devil
shake hands with the devil.author: Roméo Dallaire
shake hands with the devil.why: The UN commander's firsthand account of the Rwandan genocide; excellent and sobering.
